events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Silly Sad Strange Humanity
events.description:
Every single person has had some sad and kinda awful stuff happen to them. Also some funny stuff. Also some stuff they don't know how to feel about. Let's share in the totality of how varied and strange it is to be a human!

After meeting one another and settling in, we’ll spend most of our time on an activity where you get to see others and be seen one layer (or more?) deeper than you might normally. This one's sweet, and tender, and funny, and...I think it's easier for me to like you now.

Doors open at 7 and close at 7:15 sharp; please be there before 7:15 to participate in this one.
About your facilitator

Raven is a facilitator and curriculum builder at Sleepawake. She brings almost a decade of somatic, relational, and emotional work to the room. Previously a medic, filmmaker, tech worker, and hardcore meditator (accumulating four months in silent meditation including a stint in a monastery in Myanmar), her work now draws from various meditation traditions: Vipassana (Goenka, Gaya House traditions) and Mahamudra (Rigdzin with Dustin DiPerna). It also incorporates teachings from Realization Process (where she's a certified teacher, trained with Judith Blackstone and Roma Hammel), the Conscious Leadership Group (she's a certified 15 Commitments Coach, trained with Jim Dethmer and Diana Chapman), and a body of work that treats emotions as energy to be welcomed rather than managed, with enjoyment as the accelerator of change. Having worked with hundreds of people, Raven knows the stuff we most want to skip is usually the stuff worth staying with, and she makes this difficult task feel like a bold and wild ride.
For anyone who wants to access more personal freedom, to be honest about what they want, and to turn the most "bad" and difficult aspects of themselves into allies and heroes - Raven's got you.
At home in Berkeley, you might find her hanging out with her beautiful besties, playing narrative-driven video games and getting absolutely shredded at the gym.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Conflict as a Compass
events.description:
The strongest relationships aren't conflict avoidant; they're skilled and practiced at repair.
Ever find yourself flailing when a relationship is in conflict — robotically reciting Nonviolent Communication scripts, giving in and abandoning yourself, or walking away?
Conflict, when held a certain way, can be a clear signal of what we want for ourselves and the people we love. Its pain can be a motivating and energizing force, pointing us towards deeper, more honest relationships with ourselves and others. It's simple, but not always easy.

"Sleepawake challenged me to be more real than I ever have been, and guided me towards acting radically in alignment with my truth. It's not at all easy, but the more I do this, the more I feel like my life is ripe with possibility."
You'll leave this workshop with:
A new framework for understanding what conflict is, why it comes up, and how it can improve (rather than destroy) relationships
Real practice diving into building understanding and repair, in a real conflict that's present in your life (up to you how spicy you want to go)
A set of tools you can bring to future difficult conversations without sounding like a robot trying to say the right thing to make the conflict go away
Whether you're a Sleepawake alum or never attended one of our events, this workshop is for you if you're wanting to expand your relational toolbox to include real, authentic, vulnerable, unscripted conflict repair.
This workshop will be adapted directly from our Conflict module at Sleepawake Immersive, our weeklong intensive program. We'll spend just enough time on theory to understand the territory we're entering, and then we'll spend the majority of the time on interactive exercises including journaling, small group work, and full-group discussion.


If you'd like to do this workshop in person with friends, you'll have the option to do the small group work portion together. You're just as welcome to come on your own; this workshop is designed for you to build skills that will support all your relationships beyond this evening.
In order to maintain an intimate group for this event with enough space for facilitated group discussion, we will be capping admission.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Freezestylin'
events.description:
Creativity isn’t limited to our abilities to paint a nice picture or dance in the coolest way — it’s the skill underlying innovation. Fundamentally, it is the ability to build something out of nothing, whether that thing is a product or a business or a song you sing in the shower.
You’ll leave this event with quicker and easier access to your creative prowess — which you can channel directly into any part of your life in need of creative problem solving.
This night is designed for laughter and curiosity, not performing or being "good" at art.

“Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up.” - Picasso
As children, all of us knew how to sing and dance and draw without worrying about whether it was good enough. As we grow up, most of us learn to censor our own creative impulses, only building when we are confident we can create something good. In doing so, we block ourselves off from our own creative abilities, and lose out on our grandest ideas and innovations.
Tonight, we’ll use the voice as our medium to train our long-unused creative muscles. We’ll start gently. Although all of us knew as children how to sing and dance like no one’s watching, most of us have now learned that we have to be good at creativity in order to be comfortable accessing it. Through wordplay, rhythm, and singing games, we’ll slowly open to the possibility that we can create badly (and to the fun that ensues) — which, counterintuitively, unblocks more access to our creativity and our ability to create well.
This is not built for professional artists — this event is for people who are excited about the idea of having more access to creative thinking in their day-to-day lives, and who are open to (and probably also intimidated by) the idea of rapping or singing as part of structured games in a group of amateurs.
“Remember, before you can be great, you’ve got to be good. Before you can be good, you’ve got to be bad. But before you can even be bad, you’ve got to try.” - Art Williams
Everything we offer at this event will be opt-in. We will never make you get up on stage in front of everyone — we’ll never push you to doing any part of this that you don’t want to do. This night is for you, and we are in full support of your choices about how you’d like to participate.
Our facilitation team has been running this event for over four years, and they are familiar with both the joy and the fear that people often feel around creative expression.
Agenda
Settling in & short introduction to creative access as a trainable skill
Individual freestyle word-play games — no one will be listening to you
Group-based low-stakes voice and rhythm games — focused on the joy of what’s created, whether good or terrible
Group-based singing games — sweet, gentle, and facilitated by our team to support you in participating to exactly whatever extent you’d like to
Open-ended time to hang out and join or listen to a jam session
Logistics
There are limited spots at this event, and we will not take walk-ins if it sells out — we have a specific cap on attendance so that we can accommodate breakout groups with our facilitation team
You may want a water bottle; no need to bring anything else
Please arrive on time and plan to stay for the duration of the event; the evening is a full arc where each activity builds on the previous one
Come solo or with friends

events.name: The Founding Debate Reading Group #8 - A Compact or a Nation?
events.description:
A Compact or a Nation?
In 2026, the United States turns 250. Across eight weeks we're reading the founders in their own words — the arguments they had with each other about liberty, power, and the system of government they were building.
The question in our final week: what is the thing the Constitution made - a compact among sovereign states, or a nation? And did the experiment hold?
Washington's Farewell Address (1796) — the first president declines a third term, which was the most consequential thing he ever did, and then warns against the two forces he thinks will break the Union: party spirit and sectional feeling.
The Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions (1798–99) — twenty-six months later, his own Secretary of State and the man who drafted his first inaugural answer him. The Constitution is a compact, the states are the parties, and each may judge for itself when it has been broken. Kentucky supplies the word: nullification. Written in a good cause — the Alien and Sedition Acts were a disgrace — and it becomes the constitutional argument for secession.
The Corner-Stone speech (1861) — three weeks before Fort Sumter, the Vice-President of the Confederacy explains what his government is founded on. He does not claim the founders. He says they believed slavery was wrong in principle, that they rested their government on the equality of men, and that in believing so they were mistaken.
The Gettysburg Address (1863) — 272 words that date the nation to 1776 rather than 1787, and to the Declaration rather than the Constitution. Lincoln agrees with Stephens about what the founders believed and disagrees about whether they were right. Both men are claiming the same fathers.
The Second Inaugural (1865) — the same man, six weeks from death, with the war effectively won, declining to claim the vindication that was by then in his hands.
Download this week's reader here: masonmelead.com/foundingwk8.pdf

events.name: Voice Agents in Production — NYC Builders Meetup
events.description:
Voice AI has moved fast from impressive demos to real-world deployment - and that is where the interesting problems begin.
Voice Agents in Production is a small, technical meetup for founders, engineers, AI builders, and operators working on or exploring real-time voice agents.
The focus is practical: what actually happens when voice agents start speaking with real customers.
We’ll get into topics such as:
Real-time latency and conversation quality
Interruptions, turn-taking, and natural dialogue
Tool calling and connecting agents to real systems
Telephony and production infrastructure
Reliability, monitoring, and evaluation
Multilingual voice agents
What works in demos but breaks in production
Where Voice AI is heading next
The evening will feature a few short live demos from builders, an open discussion around lessons from building Voice AI systems, and plenty of time to meet others working in the space.
Format
5:00–5:25 PM — Arrivals & networking
5:25–5:35 PM — Welcome & introductions
5:35–6:05 PM — Voice Agents in Production: builder discussion
6:05–6:30 PM — Live demos
6:30–7:00 PM — Open discussion & networking
No long presentations and no sales pitches — just builders sharing what they are learning, showing what they are building, and meeting others working on the next generation of conversational AI.
Hosted by Kaleem Khan, Founder of heyfon.ai, while in NYC connecting with the Voice AI and broader AI builder community.
Free to attend. Registration approval required due to limited capacity.

events.name: Data Salon: AI and Labor
events.description:
An event series for fostering thought leadership across data disciplines and those who work closely with data practitioners. This event will go beyond the hype and inspect the potential impact of AI on labor from well-informed business perspectives both on the ground and systemic.
MC'd by Akpanoluo Etteh, Sr. Director of Data Engineering at Arcspan (fmr: Anthropic, Bandcamp) and founder of The Soundshop music salon series, and co-hosted by Michael Bartoli, Founder of Newtown Analytics (fmr: obé Fitness)
Details on our speakers below:

Emil's Remarks:
The future of AI is not predetermined; systems engineers/ entrepreneurs have choices, eg, about how to design technical systems that put people at the center. I will share my opinions about best practices in human-AI hybrid systems designs, at scale. 

About Emil:
Chronologically: quantitative psychology -> computational sociology -> chemicals and grocery supply chain machine learning -> climate finance entrepreneur -> hybrid human-AI knowledge systems engineer. Whoa! I design complex systems that model complex system, with applications in corporate forecasting.
Ben's remarks:
• My role at KUNGFU
• Some speculation about the future of work (i.e., things like Baumol’s cost disease, work becoming more relational, rate of change, etc)
• But specifically, what are common challenges facing organizations today?
• How human-machine teaming is one approach to solving these challenges
• Some of the qualities that matter the most today and going forward (e.g., ethical judgement)  effective leadership
• What does it mean to be a good data practitioner today?

About Ben:
Ben Szuhaj is an AI strategist passionate about helping organizations navigate AI transformation. At KUNGFU.AI, Ben works with leaders to develop and implement practical AI strategies that deliver tangible business value. Ben holds a BA in English and human-centered design from Dartmouth College, where he won the Mecklin Prize for creative nonfiction, and is a competitive long-distance runner.

events.name: Builders NYC: Dev Talk LIVE
events.description:
Dev Talk LIVE
Come hear what NYC builders are actually working on.
Dev Talk LIVE brings together a small lineup of developers, founders, and builders to showcase what they’ve built, tell the story behind it, and break down the technical and product decisions that got them there.
Each featured builder gets the floor to take us inside their project: what they set out to build, the problems they ran into, the technology behind it, what changed along the way, and what they learned from shipping it. Then we open things up for questions and conversation with the room.
No endless panels. No surface-level startup pitches. No pretending everything went perfectly.
Just builders talking builds.
We’ll have roughly 90–95 minutes of featured Dev Talks, with plenty of breathing room between sessions and time before and after to meet other developers, founders, creatives, and technologists from around NYC.

Whether you’re working on your own product, looking for inspiration, interested in how other people approach building, or just want to meet more people making cool things in NYC, come through.

events.name: Brderless Buildathon: AI Agents
events.description:
Brderless Buildathon: AI Agents - NYC
Most hackathons end at the demo. We built this differently.
The Brderless Buildathon is a two-part format: a curated 24-hour build in New York, then two weeks to keep shipping, then a Demo Day where the selected winning teams show a real product.
Part 1 - The Buildathon (October 4)
100 vetted builders. One theme: AI agents that do real work - planning, tool use, multi-step execution, human-in-the-loop. Not chatbots.
The day:
10:00am: Doors open, breakfast
11:00am: Keynote from speakers & team formation
12:00pm: Lunch & build
3:00pm: Project check-ins
4:00pm: Submissions close & final selections
5:00pm: Judging round one, awards, and selection of the teams advancing to Part 2
Food and caffeine for the full 24. Top teams advance to part 2.
Part 2 - Demo Day (October 8)
Selected teams get two weeks and mentor support + credits to turn the weekend into a product. Then they demo live to a curated room of investors, operators, and sponsors - 7-min demo, 5-min Q&A.
Who should apply?
Engineers, technical founders, AI/agents engineers, and product people who ship. Solo, with a team, or matched with one - all fine. If you come as a pair or group, please make sure that everyone registers.
About the Hosts & Sponsors
Brderless brings together the most extraordinary founders and builders through a carefully curated community.

Who Attends:
Founders & startups
PR & Agency teams
Venture Capitalists
Consultants
Finance professionals
Content & social media marketers
Marketing technology professionals
Attendance is limited to help keep conversations meaningful, so please apply for a spot. We look forward to meeting you!
About Our Meet Ups:
Our Meet Ups are relaxed, industry-agnostic gatherings built for professionals who want to unplug from the standard corporate routine and connect on a human level. Whether you are looking to exchange fresh perspectives, brainstorm new concepts, or simply meet peers navigating similar spaces, this environment is designed for open-ended conversation and organic relationship-building.
What It Is:
An open, welcoming community space to meet new connections.
An opportunity to exchange industry perspectives and uncover unexpected collaborations.
A low-pressure, welcoming atmosphere with no formal agenda or mandatory pitches.
What It Isn’t:
RTM Nexus Meet Up is not a curated buyer/seller event and is not structured around guaranteed access to a specific target audience, vertical, company type, or decision-maker profile (ICP).
Looking for something more targeted? If you need to connect with a specific niche—such as retail, fashion, beauty, CPG, or enterprise brand leaders—check out our "Retail Leaders Receptions" and "Nexus Mixers" instead. Those events are intentionally curated and sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

NYC IRL community for advanced practitioners of LLM coding techniques. Monthly Brooklyn meetups on the new moon.. 

The CEG emphasizes advanced use of LLMs for the working engineer, and is not intended for first time coders.

We start with a lecture on whats happened in the last month, then have some guided or group discussions about current trends in tooling and capabilities. 

 CEG posts at https://x.com/ContextGuildNYC

Bring your main coding laptop so we can share how we build together.
